title: Insight Learning & Field Theory: Köhler & Lewin
description: Analyze Köhler's chimpanzee experiments on Tenerife, 'Aha!' problem-solving, and Lewin's social field theory.

slides.title: Wolfgang Köhler on Tenerife: Sultan's Insight 🍌
slides.content:
# Challenging Trial-and-Error

During World War I, German psychologist **Wolfgang Köhler** (1887–1967) was marooned at the Prussian Academy of Sciences research station on the Canary Island of Tenerife.

Köhler tested problem-solving abilities in chimpanzees, particularly an exceptionally clever ape named **Sultan**.

### Thorndike vs. Köhler
* Thorndike claimed animals only learn through mechanical, blind trial-and-error (stamping in responses over hundreds of trials).
* Köhler placed bananas outside the cage, just out of reach, and gave Sultan two hollow bamboo poles that were each too short.
* After pacing and pondering, Sultan suddenly had an **'Aha!' experience**: he jammed the thinner pole into the hollow end of the wider pole, created a single long stick, and reeled in the fruit in one smooth, deliberate motion!

Köhler called this **Insight Learning (*Einsicht*)**: the sudden perceptual restructuring of the problem field that leads directly to a solution.

quizData.question: How did Wolfgang Köhler's concept of 'insight learning' differ from Thorndike's trial-and-error learning?

options.text: Insight learning involves sudden mental restructuring of the problem rather than blind repetitive trial-and-error
Insight learning occurs only after electric shock punishment
Insight learning is limited to humans with language
Insight learning requires continuous external positive reinforcement

quizData.explanation: Köhler demonstrated that chimpanzees solve problems through cognitive restructuring of the environmental field, experiencing sudden insight.

slides.title: Kurt Lewin & Field Theory 🌐
slides.content:
# The Father of Social Psychology

**Kurt Lewin** (1890–1947) applied Gestalt principles beyond visual perception to human motivation, personality, and group behavior.

Borrowing concepts from physics (magnetic fields), Lewin introduced **Field Theory**:

### Lewin's Famous Equation
$$B = f(P, E)$$

* **Behavior ($B$)** is a function ($f$) of the **Person ($P$)** interacting with their subjective psychological **Environment ($E$)**.

Lewin called this totality the **Life Space**: the psychological field containing all past memories, present goals, valence barriers, and perceived possibilities influencing the individual at any given moment.

### Major Contributions of Lewin
* **Leadership Styles**: Conducted famous studies contrasting Autocratic, Democratic, and Laissez-faire leadership.
* **Group Dynamics**: Coined the term 'group dynamics', showing that groups are living Gestalts with emergent properties.
* **Action Research**: Pioneered research designed to solve real social problems (racial prejudice, workplace democracy).

slides.title: The Zeigarnik Effect ☕
slides.content:
## Unfinished Tasks Stick in the Mind

While sitting in a Berlin cafe with Kurt Lewin, student **Bluma Zeigarnik** noticed that waiters remembered complex unpaid food orders with photographic precision—yet completely forgot the order the second the bill was paid!

Zeigarnik empirically demonstrated the **Zeigarnik Effect**: uncompleted tasks create psychological tension within the life space, leading to significantly higher memory recall than finished tasks.
